birth.place: Munzingen, Freiburg im Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg, Germany

occupation: Mason / stone mason (Munzingen citizen and mason 1862; stone mason Hazleton 1870, 1880)
summary: John's 3rd great-grandfather; a stone mason born in the wine village of Munzingen near Freiburg, who brought his family to Hazleton, PA about 1868.
bio:
Friedrich Mayer was born early on 2 Mar 1835 at Munzingen (Amt Freiburg, Baden), 'legitimate son of Heinrich Mayer, local citizen and mason, and of [Ju]liana Senn' (L 10 Nr. 1590, births 1835 No. 10, fol. 100). The Meier-line reader gives baptism the same day; the German-origins reader read the dates as born 2 Mar, baptized/recorded 8 Mar 1835, and read the mother's surname as 'B[onn?]' under an ink blot — 'Senn' is preferred because the 1862 marriage names Juliana Senn. Godmother: Maria Anna, wife of the teacher Johann Schell (also a witness); signed by Pfarrer Faller. The FamilySearch tree's 'Freiburg' birthplace is the archdiocese, not the town. He was one of at least ten children of Heinrich and Juliana. Like his father he became a mason and a citizen (Bürger) of Munzingen before 1862. On 20 Oct 1862 he married Maria Anna Birkenmaier at Munzingen (L 10 Nr. 1591, Ehebuch 1862 No. 2, p. 205): 'Friedrich Mayer, born here 2 March 1835, Catholic, citizen and mason here, legitimate single son of the local citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and of Juliana Senn' and 'Maria Anna Birkenmaier, born here 29 March 1837, legitimate single daughter of the late local citizen and master joiner (Schreinermeister) Servaz Birkenmaier and of Agatha Heizler'; licence from the Grand-Ducal Landamt Freiburg 2 Oct 1862; banns 12 and 19 Oct; witnesses Joseph [Wenz?] and [Fr. Anton Schumann?], both citizens and master shoemakers (uncertain readings); only two marriages in Munzingen that year. Their son Frederick was born 11 Nov 1862 in Germany. No emigration note was found in the margins of the 1835 or 1862 entries. The family — Friedrich (~32), Maria (~30), and four children Friedrich, Franziska, Maria and Heinrich — emigrated between Nov 1866 and Sept 1869, probably 1868 (Henry's 1910 census; other children's census entries give 1867 or 1868); no matching group in the Bremen DAD 1866–69, so possibly via Le Havre or Antwerp. In the 1870 census (Hazleton Borough East Ward, p. 42, 8 Jun 1870) he was 'Meyer, Frederick, 35, stone mason, born Baden', not yet a citizen, with Anna 33, Frederick 8, 'Francisco' [Frances] 7, Maria 6, Henry 4 (all Baden) and Clarissa, infant born PA (Sept); next door was Anthony Werner, 51, also a Baden stone mason. In 1880 (Hazleton East Ward 1st Dist., ED 137, p. 13, 11 Jun 1880, dwelling 111, family 133) he was 'Myer, Friedrich, 45, stone mason, born Baden, both parents Baden', with Annie 43, Fred 18 (coal-mine laborer), Frances 17, Mary 15, Henry 14 (at school, born Baden), Fressa 11 (born PA), Elizabeth 8, Annie 5, Aggathe 3, and brother-in-law Gabriel Bergenmyer, 29, gardener, sick with 'fever & ague'. A 'Fred. Meier' was a Democratic poor-district conferee and standing-committee member (Hazleton/Freeland poor district) in Jan 1893 — could equally be his son Fred (b. 1862). A 'Fred Meyer of Hazleton' with a little son Joseph visited Freeland in 1889 — probably a younger man. The family most likely belonged to Holy Trinity German Catholic parish, Hazleton (unverified). He died 19 Feb 1913 in Hazleton (PA death index 1913: 'Meier, Frederick; file 14339; Hazleton; Feb. 19'); a Jacob Meier also died in Hazleton on 6 Jan 1913 (file 2939), possibly kin. Burial in Hazleton per the Find a Grave index on FamilySearch ('Frederick Meier', 4K6D-BN3Z); cemetery not shown. The earlier research assumed a Kirchzarten origin (because of his wife's supposed family); he is not in the Dreisamtal database, and the family is now proven to be from Munzingen.

The Munzingen birth register for 1862 explains why Friedrich and Maria Anna married in October 1862. Their first child, Friedrich, was born on 11 Jan 1862 at 9:30 a.m. and baptized on 13 January as the illegitimate son of 'the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier', daughter of the late master joiner Servatius Birkenmaier and Agatha Heitzler. In the same entry the single mason Friedrich Mayer, son of the citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and Juliana Senn, freely declared himself the father before the priest and the witnesses. He asked that the child carry his surname and have all the rights of an acknowledged child. The godparents were family: Joseph Wenz, shoemaker of Munzingen and husband of Friedrich's sister Maria Anna Creszentia, and Friedrich's unmarried sister Sophie Mayer, then in domestic service at Freiburg ([R4-S1]). The parents married nine months later, on 20 Oct 1862. This birth date, 11 Jan 1862, matches the date the son himself gave on his 1886 Luzerne marriage docket ('11 January 1862', Hazleton) ([R4-S2]), and it corrects the tree's 11 Nov 1862.

In America the family's spelling kept shifting. Friedrich's eldest son appears as 'Fred Meir' in 1886 ([R4-S2]), and probably as 'Fred Meires' of Hazleton in the 1915 state death index (see Frederick Meier). Friedrich's own son Henry J. died in Wilkes-Barre on 20 Dec 1950, not in 1940 (see Henry J. Meier).

events.description: Son Friedrich born 11 Jan 1862 to the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier. Before the parish priest and witnesses, the single mason Friedrich Mayer, legitimate son of the citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and Juliana Senn, declared himself the father and asked that the child bear his surname with full rights. Godparents: Joseph Wenz, shoemaker (his brother-in-law), and Sophie Mayer, of age, single, in service at Freiburg, daughter of Heinrich Mayer. [R4-S1]

facts.label: Surname
facts.value: Surname spelling history (Mayer→Meier): Munzingen registers write Mayer 1820–1862 (1820 marriage 'Henericus Mayer', 1835 birth 'Friedrich Mayer', 1862 marriage 'Friedrich Mayer'); 1870 US census 'Meyer, Frederick'; 1880 census 'Myer, Friedrich'; the 1892 Luzerne marriage docket No. 11054 is the first record spelling it 'Meier' (Henry J. Meier) — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it; 'Meier' is consistent from 1910 on (1910, 1920, 1926, 1930, 1950 records; PA death indexes 1911/1913/1963) except 'Meyer, Henry J.' in the 1940 census; no formal name change is recorded.

openQuestions: PA death certificate 1913 #14339 — parents, birthplace, burial ground, informant.
Emigration file (Auswanderungsakten, Bezirksamt Freiburg) at Staatsarchiv Freiburg; Le Havre/Antwerp → New York lists 1867–68 under 'Mayer'.
Hazleton cemetery (Holy Trinity German Catholic? St. Gabriel's?).
Was Jacob Meier (d. 6 Jan 1913 Hazleton, file 2939) a relative?

Emigration still not found. The Munzingen 1862 birth and marriage entries carry no emigration note in what was read. The Auswanderungsakten of Bezirksamt Freiburg (Staatsarchiv Freiburg) for 1867–68 remain the best lead.
Order PA death certificate 1913 no. 14339 (as before).

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Name in the Ancestry tree: "Freiderich Meier"; research uses "Friedrich Mayer".
Round 4 relationship evidence (child I282608085066, proven): 1862 Munzingen birth: Friedrich Mayer acknowledges paternity of Friedrich, b. 11 Jan 1862, son of Maria Anna Birkenmaier
Round 4 searched without result: Munzingen death indexes 1862, 1863, 1865, 1866, 1867 (L 10 Nr. 1591): no Heinrich Mayer (for father's death)

Round 4: found the 11 Jan 1862 Munzingen birth of son Friedrich to Maria Anna Birkenmaier, with Friedrich's paternity acknowledgment (the reason for the Oct 1862 marriage); godparents his sister Sophie and brother-in-law Joseph Wenz.

funFacts: His first son was born nine months before the wedding. Friedrich went to the priest two days after the birth to acknowledge the boy as his own, and his sister and brother-in-law stood as godparents.
